description: Ytterbium is a chemical element with symbol Yb and atomic number 70. It is a soft, malleable and ductile metal that is the fourteenth element in the lanthanide series, distinguished by the relative stability of its +2 oxidation state and its closed-shell electron configuration.
uses: Ytterbium is mainly used as a dopant of stainless steel or active laser media, and less often as a gamma ray source. Microscopic traces are used as a dopant in the Yb:YAG laser, and some ytterbium halides are used as reagents in organic synthesis, tooth fillings, and X-ray contrast agents.
characteristics: Ytterbium is a rare-earth element with notably lower density, melting point, and boiling point than most other lanthanides due to its closed-shell electron configuration. It has a melting point of 824°C and boiling point of 1196°C, is readily dissolved by strong mineral acids, tarnishes slowly in air taking on a golden or brown hue, and forms both divalent and trivalent compounds, with the divalent state being unusual for lanthanides.
